claims.text: The retrieved official uv documentation defines freshness against project metadata: adding a dependency or excluding its locked version makes the lock stale; a constraint change that still admits the locked version need not. New upstream releases alone do not make a lock stale. `uv lock --check` checks freshness and is equivalent to --locked on other commands. These are current online documentation semantics, not verification of an installed uv version.
`uv sync --locked` requires an up-to-date lockfile and leaves it unchanged. If missing or needing an update, uv exits with an error rather than updating it.

`uv sync --frozen` skips freshness checking and uses locked versions without updating the lockfile. A missing lockfile is an error. Dependency additions in pyproject.toml that were never locked will be absent from the environment.

Neither flag alone guarantees no network: their documented scope is lockfile handling. The separate --offline option disables uv network access and restricts it to cached data and local files; it does not promise successful installation when required inputs are unavailable locally.

`uv sync` defaults to exact synchronization, removing extraneous packages. Use --inexact to retain extras already installed. This choice is independent of freshness checking. Dependency groups and optional extras still determine what is selected for installation; the dev group is included by default, and --no-dev excludes it.

The official Docker guide demonstrates --frozen for an intermediate workspace dependency layer lacking project metadata, followed by --locked after all workspace members are copied. This supports the recommendation below; no actual production environment was inspected or tested.

evidence.locator: Intermediate layers in workspaces; explanation at retrieved line 554

note.recommendation: Recommendation: commit and review uv.lock; make the final production sync use --locked with complete project/workspace metadata, keeping default exact synchronization in a dedicated environment. Select runtime groups/extras explicitly; --no-dev excludes dev but does not necessarily exclude other configured default groups. Reserve --frozen for deliberately incomplete intermediate layers, then validate with a final --locked sync. Add --offline when uv must avoid network, after provisioning required local inputs; do not treat locked/frozen as offline switches. Pin and validate the deployment's uv version. This is policy advice inferred from the cited semantics, not a tested deployment recipe.
